content.title: About
content.content: Reduced‑fat oatmeal cookie is a light, crunchy snack made from whole oat flakes, whole‑grain flour, a modest amount of vegetable oil and sweeteners. The recipe omits raisins, making it suitable for those who avoid dried fruit.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oat flakes retain most of the fiber and beta‑glucans beneficial for heart health.
The cookies are baked at a lower temperature, preserving a crisp texture without excess oil.
Fat reduction is achieved by replacing part of the oil with apple puree, keeping moisture.
The product contains no artificial colors or flavors.
Oatmeal cookies are often used in weight‑loss meal plans.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Oat flakes provide soluble fiber that helps regulate blood glucose levels.

items.title: Low fat content
items.content: Reduced oil makes the cookie less caloric than traditional versions.

items.title: Contains beta‑glucans
items.content: Beta‑glucans support cholesterol reduction and immune function.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Oats supply thiamine, niacin and folate, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Digestive support
items.content: Fiber promotes intestinal motility and regular bowel movements.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: The product contains wheat, so it is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although refined sugar is reduced, a small amount of sweetener remains.

items.title: Risk of over‑consumption
items.content: The crunchy texture may lead to rapid eating of large portions.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the cookie as a standalone snack, crumble it into yogurt or muesli, or use it as a base for dessert tartlets. Keep it dry to maintain crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cookies in an airtight container at room temperature, away from direct sunlight. For extended shelf life, refrigerate to prevent moisture absorption.
